summary: Brick lighthouse on Keweenaw Bay, Lake Superior, lit 10 August 1878; keeper John B. Crebassa served 30 years; automated in 1922.

lens.type: fifth-order Fresnel by L. Sautter & Co., France

structures.type: square brick tower with octagonal lantern
structures.note: 32 ft from base to centre of lantern (USLHS); 36 ft 6 in from base to ventilator ball (LighthouseFriends).
Red-brick one-and-a-half-storey dwelling; owned by the Keweenaw Bay Indian Community.

access.note: Sources disagree: USLHS 'Open to Public: Yes'; LighthouseFriends 'Grounds open, dwelling/tower closed'; Mining Gazette (2024) 'not open to the public'.

events.note: Tower and dwelling built from August 1877 (work) to 1878
First lit 10 August 1878 by keeper John B. Crebassa
Lighthouse jacked up and moved back 200 ft from the shore because of erosion; a hemlock wall and sand fill were added
Inspector Oliver G. Brown recommended a privy chimney and warned that beach erosion put the dwelling in danger
Tower light replaced by an acetylene light on a 35 ft pipe mast beside a brick tank house 37 yards east of the lighthouse; focal plane 35 ft, white flash every three seconds
Lighthouse and surrounding property bought by the Keweenaw Bay Indian Community

keepers.name: John B. Crebassa
keepers.note: Sole keeper from first lighting (1878) to his death. The L'Anse Sentinel obituary (printed 7 March 1908) gives the death as 'Sunday afternoon last, March 1st, 1906'; 1 March 1908 was a Sunday and 1 March 1906 was not, so the year is taken as 1908; LighthouseFriends has him die three days after a 27 February 1908 Sentinel article. Earlier keeper at Portage Entry 1865 to 1878 (1883 county history; obituary). LighthouseFriends calls that station Portage River Lighthouse.

other_stations.name: Portage Entry light (LighthouseFriends: Portage River Lighthouse)

keepers.name: Anna Crebassa
keepers.note: Kept the light a few weeks at the opening of navigation in 1908 (LighthouseFriends); USLHS lists her as principal keeper 1908-1908. The obituary names his wife as Hannah Wilbon; see resolved_conflicts.

keepers.name: Thomas G. Thomson
keepers.note: USLHS spells Thomson; LighthouseFriends text spells Thompson. Transferred in from the Eagle Harbor Range Lights (LighthouseFriends). A 1917 Sentinel item prints a letter from him from Eureka, California, saying he had been keeper at Sand Point and most recently was stationed at Loleta, California.

keepers.name: Richard Thompson
keepers.note: LighthouseFriends calls him the fourth keeper of the light

resolved_conflicts.field: John B. Crebassa, date of death
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The L'Anse Sentinel of 7 March 1908 prints the death as 'Sunday afternoon last, March 1st, 1906'. 1 March 1908 was a Sunday and 1 March 1906 was a Thursday, so the printed year appears to be an error for 1908. LighthouseFriends says he died three days after a Sentinel article of 27 February 1908, which fits 1908. The Coast Guard's account (through the Mining Gazette) gives retirement on 1 March 1908. The story uses 1908 and says why.

The Sentinel obituary says he married Miss Hannah Wilbon of Detroit when he was 25. LighthouseFriends says his wife was Anna and that she kept the light in 1908; the USLHS roster lists Anna Crebassa as keeper 1908. Both are recorded; it is not resolved whether Anna was a second wife or an error.
The Light-House Board's 1894 report gives 86 running feet; LighthouseFriends gives 'some eighty feet'. The Board's figure is used.
USLHS: open to public; LighthouseFriends: grounds open, dwelling and tower closed; Mining Gazette (2024): not open to the public. The story reports the disagreement.
USLHS spells Thomson; LighthouseFriends spells Thompson in its text and Thomson in its roster. The USLHS spelling is used.

The 1878 lantern showed a fixed red light at 39 ft (LighthouseFriends; USLHS gives 39 ft above water); the 1922 light had a focal plane of 35 ft and a white flash every three seconds (LighthouseFriends). The record's current 'Fl W 4s' fits the 1922 light, but its focal height of 12.2 m (about 40 ft) does not match the 35 ft LighthouseFriends gives. Not changed here; flagged in notes.

The Sentinel obituary and the 1883 county history name the earlier station 'Portage Entry'; LighthouseFriends calls it 'Portage River Lighthouse'. The story uses Portage Entry, the name the two local sources give, and notes the LighthouseFriends name.

LighthouseFriends says Peter Crebassa built a trading post on the bay in 1837. The 1883 county history says Dubay had founded the American Fur Company's post and that Crebassa removed it to the east shore in 1836. The story gives the history's sequence as a separate account and does not choose between them.

LighthouseFriends says he looked after the light 'for nearly thirty-nine years'; the 1878 start and 1908 death give about thirty years; the obituary's 'forty-three years' of climbing the tower counts from 1865. The story reports the obituary figure and notes LighthouseFriends' figure.

notes_for_editor: Sources: four of the seven are secondary compilations (LighthouseFriends, a 1883 county history transcription, the Mining Gazette, the USLHS archive); the primary material is the Light-House Board's 1894 entry, two Sentinel pages on Chronicling America, and the 1883 history. The Light-House Board's reports before 1891 and the Commissioner's reports after 1922 are not in the corpus, and the 1891-1901 volumes hold only list entries for this station; I did not search for the 1863 committee or the 1873 appropriation in primary text and LighthouseFriends is the only source for them. No wreck or rescue is tied to the light in any source read. A corpus search for 'Sand Point' in the Lighthouse reports returned the Escanaba Sand Point light (Little Bay de Noquette, Green Bay), the Commissioner's 1920 entry (p. 84) and others; those are different places and are not used. Newspapers: one search (Crebassa and Sand Point, Michigan, 1878-1922) found 51 pages, mostly the L'Anse Sentinel; two were read (the 1908 obituary and the 1917 Thomson item), and only those are used. Focal height: the record's 12.2 m does not match either LighthouseFriends figure (39 ft for the 1878 lantern, 35 ft for the 1922 light); flagged, not changed. Status: the record marks the station inactive and the current light (Fl W 4s) is the 1922 light on the pipe mast; the tower is no longer the aid. Access and visiting: the sources disagree; I did not visit or verify the site. The keepers are from the USLHS roster (NARA registers) and LighthouseFriends, and none is confirmed in a primary text read here; the Sentinel confirms Crebassa's appointment at Portage Entry and his death. Louis Guy, the private owner named by LighthouseFriends, is not named in the story (a private resident, not a public figure). Thomson's Loleta posting is from a 1917 Sentinel column; the station there is not identified, so no other_stations entry is given for it. Verification 2026-10-28: the printed year of the obituary ('March 1st, 1906') comes from the OCR text of the 7 March 1908 Sentinel page and was not checked against the page image (loc.gov is reached only through newspapers.py here); the weekday (1 March 1908 was a Sunday, 1 March 1906 a Thursday) and LighthouseFriends' three-days-after-27-February account both point to 1908, but the printed year should be confirmed on the page image before publication. The 1883 county history's Portage Entry dates (1865 to 1878) and the 1894 sidewalk entry (scan p. 522, printed page unconfirmed) are OCR text as well.
